translated.evidence: XNLI (Conneau et al., 2018) is a dataset for cross-lingual Natural Language Inference, which consists of professional translations of the MNLI corpus into 14 languages.

native_annotators.evidence: Professional translators translated from English; not natively authored in target languages. The original English data was created by crowdworkers.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Translated from English MultiNLI corpus; content reflects English-language contexts and cultural references.

XNLI.annotation_quality_notes: Professional translation quality. One of the most widely used multilingual NLI benchmarks.

translated.evidence: IndicXNLI (Aggarwal et al., 2022) that translates the XNLI dataset into 11 Indic languages by using Machine Translation, followed by validation by native speakers.

native_annotators.evidence: Machine translation with validation by native speakers; native speakers validated but did not create the content.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Translated from English-origin XNLI data; inherits English cultural context despite being in Indic languages.

Indic-XNLI.annotation_quality_notes: Machine translation followed by native speaker validation. Quality depends on MT system and validation thoroughness.

translated.evidence: GLUECoS-NLI (Khanuja et al., 2020a) is a code-mixed NLI dataset in Hindi-English, consisting of Bollywood (Hindi) movie conversations as premises, with manually created hypotheses.

native_annotators.evidence: Code-mixed data from Bollywood movie conversations with manually created hypotheses, implying native Hindi-English bilingual speakers.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Premises are from Bollywood (Hindi) movie conversations, reflecting Indian cultural context and natural code-switching patterns.

GLUECoS NLI.annotation_quality_notes: Naturally occurring code-mixed data from Bollywood movies with manually created hypotheses.

translated.evidence: PAWS-X (Yang et al., 2019b) is a paraphrase identification dataset professionally translated from the PAWS dataset into six typologically diverse languages.

native_annotators.evidence: Professional translators translated from English PAWS; original content created in English.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Translated from English PAWS dataset derived from Wikipedia and Quora; content reflects English-language sources.

translated.evidence: XCOPA (Ponti et al., 2020) is a commonsense reasoning dataset, which is a translation of the COPA dataset into 11 typologically diverse languages.

native_annotators.evidence: Translation by native speakers/translators of target languages, but content originated in English.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Translated from English COPA; commonsense reasoning scenarios reflect English/Western cultural context.

XCOPA.annotation_quality_notes: Includes very low-resource languages such as Eastern Apurímac Quechua and Haitian Creole.

translated.evidence: XStoryCloze (Lin et al., 2022b) is created by translating the English StoryCloze dataset using professional translators into 10 typologically diverse languages.

native_annotators.evidence: Professional translators translated from English; original content authored in English.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Translated from English StoryCloze; story scenarios reflect English/American cultural contexts.

translated.evidence: TyDiQA (Clark et al., 2020) is a QA dataset covering 11 typologically diverse languages. Natively collected by information-seeking speakers.

native_annotators.evidence: Questions were natively created by speakers of each target language performing information-seeking tasks.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Natively collected from speakers in each language community; questions reflect genuine information needs in those languages.

TyDiQA-GoldP.annotation_quality_notes: Gold standard QA dataset with natively authored questions. MEGA evaluates on Gold-P subtask.

translated.evidence: MLQA (Lewis et al., 2020) is an extractive QA dataset translated into 7 languages by professional translators.

native_annotators.evidence: Professional translators translated from English; original QA pairs in English.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Translated from English sources; content and questions reflect English Wikipedia context.

MLQA.annotation_quality_notes: Professional translation with answer alignment via attention scores for translate-test splits.

translated.evidence: XQuAD (Artetxe et al., 2020) consists of professional translations of a subset of the SQuaD dataset into 10 languages.

native_annotators.evidence: Professional translators translated from English SQuAD; original content authored in English.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Translated from English SQuAD based on English Wikipedia articles.

XQuAD.annotation_quality_notes: Professional translation of SQuAD subset. Only validation data publicly available.

translated.evidence: IndicQA (Doddapaneni et al., 2022) is a manually curated cloze-style reading comprehension dataset... context paragraphs are chosen from Wikipedia articles whose topics are closely related to Indic culture, history, etc.

native_annotators.evidence: Manually curated by creators; context from Wikipedia articles on Indic topics, suggesting native speaker involvement.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Context paragraphs are chosen from Wikipedia articles whose topics are closely related to Indic culture, history, etc.

IndicQA.annotation_quality_notes: Manually curated cloze-style dataset. Part of IndicXTREME.

translated.evidence: UDPOS is based on Universal Dependencies treebanks containing natively-sourced text in each language with expert POS annotations.

native_annotators.evidence: Universal Dependencies treebanks are annotated by expert linguists, typically native or highly proficient speakers of each language.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Text sources vary by language; many are from native-language sources (news, literature, web), but some may use parallel or translated text.

UDPOS.annotation_quality_notes: Expert linguistic annotation following Universal Dependencies guidelines. Quality and consistency vary across languages.

translated.evidence: PANX (Pan et al., 2017) or WikiANN is a Named Entity Recognition dataset consisting of Wikipedia sentences tagged with Person, Organization and Location.

native_annotators.evidence: Annotations created via cross-lingual annotation projection, not by native speaker annotators.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Wikipedia text is in the native language, but entity annotations are projected cross-lingually and may not reflect culturally appropriate entity categorization.

WikiANN.annotation_quality_notes: Automatic cross-lingual annotation projection from Wikipedia. Quality varies significantly across languages.

translated.evidence: The WinoMT dataset consists of 3888 English sentences... We perform zero-shot monolingual prompting of all sentences in the dataset to translate them in 8 target languages.

native_annotators.evidence: English source sentences from existing datasets; translation is performed by LLMs as part of the evaluation task.

culturally_grounded.evidence: English-centric gender bias evaluation based on English occupational stereotypes (WinoGender + WinoBias).

WinoMT.annotation_quality_notes: Gender bias evaluation via MT. English source with LLM translation to target languages. Gender accuracy measured on translations.

translated.evidence: The EN-ES-CS Sentiment Analysis dataset consisting of English-Spanish Tweets, naturally occurring code-mixed data.

native_annotators.evidence: Tweets are naturally produced by bilingual speakers; sentiment annotation was done automatically using SentiStrength.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Naturally occurring code-mixed English-Spanish tweets reflecting bilingual community language use.

EN-ES-CS.annotation_quality_notes: Sentiment labels assigned automatically via SentiStrength tool, not human annotation.

translated.evidence: The Jigsaw dataset contains online comments sourced from Wikipedia. The training data, which is in English, contains labels pertaining to the toxicity of the comment. Test data in 6 languages.

native_annotators.evidence: INSUFFICIENT_INFO: The MEGA paper does not specify whether annotation of multilingual test data involved native speakers.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Training data in English from Wikipedia; multilingual test data sourced from Wikipedia in target languages but toxicity framework is English-centric.

Jigsaw.annotation_quality_notes: Crowdsourced toxicity labels. English training data with multilingual test sets.

translated.evidence: The XLSum dataset contains article-summary pairs across 44 typologically diverse languages. Natively authored BBC news content.

native_annotators.evidence: BBC journalists write articles and summaries in each language for their respective language services.

culturally_grounded.evidence: BBC news articles are written for specific language communities by journalists serving those communities; content reflects local and regional topics.

XLSum.annotation_quality_notes: Professional journalism quality. Naturally occurring article-summary pairs from BBC services in 44 languages.
